subject: SaaSify: sudden spike in generation errors — possible SDK/streaming issue
messages:
From: Jordan Pierce <jordan@saasify.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate from /v1/generate (streaming) — urgent

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a big increase in errors across our production fleet this morning after a rollout of our integration using the Redwood client SDK (v1.4.2). Key observations:
- ~8% of streaming requests to /v1/generate are returning truncated or "invalid chunk" errors.
- p95 latency climbed from ~220ms to ~1.1s over the 06:00-09:00 PT window.
- Errors are concentrated on endpoints using streaming (we call setStreaming(true) in the SDK). Non-streaming requests look normal.

Attached: logs.zip (server-side request/response traces), p99_latency_chart.png.

Repro: we can reproduce locally by opening a streaming request and waiting ~700-1200ms; the client reports a parsing error and the server logs show an abrupt connection reset.

This is impacting multiple customers — can we get a priority triage? If this is infrastructure-related we'll need exec attention quickly.

— Jordan
Ops, SaaSify

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Pierce <jordan@saasify.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate from /v1/generate (streaming) — urgent

Jordan — thanks for the quick flag and the artifacts. I've escalated to our engineering and CS leads (cc'd).
Immediate plan:
1) Monica and I will coordinate a short incident bridge (15m) to validate the impact and collect correlation IDs.
2) Vivek will run a dive on the traces you've sent to check for transport/parser issues.
3) We'll propose a short mitigation (server-side toggle) you can apply without redeploying your stack.

Can you send 2-3 example correlation ids from logs.zip (single-line) and confirm whether all affected clients are on SDK v1.4.2?

Rishi
Account Lead — Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate from /v1/generate (streaming) — urgent

Quick triage notes after initial trace review (attached snippet: patch.diff):
- Root cause hypothesis: malformed streaming payloads created by client-side SDK v1.4.2 when using the streaming parser. Two issues observed in traces:
  1) Some client requests include both "Content-Length" and "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" headers. Our HTTP layer treats this as ambiguous; some proxies/servers favor Content-Length leading to early stream termination.
  2) The SDK streaming helper can emit an extra CRLF before chunk boundaries when the payload includes a top-level JSON metadata header. That pattern produces an empty chunk which our streaming parser currently treats as a fatal framing error ("invalid chunk length").
- Repro locally by curling a handcrafted request with both headers or with an extra CRLF inserted; parser fails "invalid chunk" within 700-1200ms similar to customer traces.
- Short-term mitigation (server-side): strip duplicate Content-Length when Transfer-Encoding: chunked present and accept empty chunks as no-ops for ~72h while we push a client patch. This is a small change in our streaming ingress and can be rolled without infra changes.
- Long-term: publish patch to SDK v1.4.3 that removes duplicate header emission and hardens the streaming helper to ignore spurious CRLFs between chunks. Target release: 2026-05-01 (48 hours).

I'll prepare a minimal server-side rule (one-line config) and a backport patch to staging now. Attaching patch.diff (proposed server strip + SDK fix snippet).

Vivek
Senior Software Engineer — Inference Runtime

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Pierce <jordan@saasify.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary workaround and next steps

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the reports. Quick mitigation you can try now without changing your SDK or redeploying:

1) Toggle streaming parser off on your account as a workaround (server-side flag):
   curl -X POST \n     https://api.redwood.ai/admin/flags \n     -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>' \n     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n     -d '{"account":"saasify","enable_streaming_parser":false}'

2) Or call the non-streaming endpoint /v1/generate?stream=false for critical paths.

We expect this to reduce parsing errors immediately (client will get buffered response; higher memory but avoids chunk framing errors). Vivek's team is pushing the SDK patch and a server-side tolerant rule this afternoon.

Please confirm after making the flag change; share a fresh correlation id and we'll monitor in our incident dashboard.

— Monica
Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Pierce <jordan@saasify.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary workaround and next steps

Monica — toggled enable_streaming_parser=false at 11:30 PT. Immediate impact: error rate dropped from ~8% to ~0.8% and p95 latency returned near baseline. Thank you for the quick workaround.

Two asks from our side:
1) Permanent fix timeline and whether SDK v1.4.3 will be considered a breaking change for us.
2) Given the customer impact (multiple paying customers affected during the morning window) we need to discuss SLA credits and would like an executive contact for that conversation.

Jordan
Senior Ops Engineer — SaaSify

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2026 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: FWD: SaaSify streaming parser incident — exec ask for SLA credits

Markus — forwarding a thread that started 4/28. Summary:
- Impact: SaaSify saw ~8% streaming request errors for ~3 hours; customer toggled streaming parser off and errors dropped to ~0.8%.
- Cause: client SDK v1.4.2 emitted duplicate headers and an extra CRLF in chunked streaming mode; our streaming parser treated empty chunks as fatal. Vivek proposes a server-side tolerant rule (deployed) + SDK patch v1.4.3 (target 2026-05-01).
- Customer asks: exec contact for SLA credits and confirmation of permanent fix timeline.

Attachments: metrics_summary.pdf (impact), p99_latency_chart.png.

Recommendation: offer a goodwill credit (we usually do 5-15% for incidents with customer-visible errors) and schedule an exec call with SaaSify CPO to confirm roadmap and timeline. Requesting your sign-off.

Thanks,
Rishi
